questions.text: Which of the following is a characteristic of all living things?
questions.explanation: All living things respond to stimuli (irritability). Movement, photosynthesis and hibernation are not shown by all living things.

questions.text: The organelle responsible for energy production in the cell is the ___.
questions.explanation: The mitochondrion is the site of aerobic respiration, which releases energy as ATP.

questions.text: Which of the following structures is found in plant cells but NOT in animal cells?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll for photosynthesis, occur in plant cells but not in animal cells.

questions.text: Bacteria belong to the kingdom ___.
questions.explanation: In the five-kingdom classification, the prokaryotes (bacteria and blue-green algae) form the kingdom Monera.

questions.text: Which of the following organisms is a fungus?
questions.explanation: Rhizopus (bread mould) is a fungus. Spirogyra is an alga, while Euglena and Paramecium are protists.

questions.text: The bryophytes are distinguished from the pteridophytes by the absence of ___.
questions.explanation: Mosses (bryophytes) lack true xylem and phloem, whereas ferns (pteridophytes) possess vascular tissues.

questions.text: Countershading in fish is an adaptation for ___.
questions.explanation: Countershading (dark above, light below) breaks up the fish's outline and camouflages it from predators.

questions.text: In a termite colony, the caste responsible for reproduction is the ___.
questions.explanation: The king and queen are the reproductive caste; workers and soldiers are sterile.

questions.text: In a transverse section of a dicotyledonous stem, the vascular bundles are arranged in a ___.
questions.explanation: In dicot stems the vascular bundles form a ring; in monocot stems they are scattered.

questions.text: The tissue that provides flexibility and support in young plant stems is ___.
questions.explanation: Collenchyma is a living supporting tissue that gives flexible strength; sclerenchyma is rigid and dead at maturity.

questions.text: Photosynthesis takes place in the ___.
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis occurs in the chloroplast, where chlorophyll traps sunlight.

questions.text: Which of the following is a macro-element required by plants?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen is required in large amounts (a macro-element). Zinc, boron and copper are micro-elements needed in tiny amounts.

questions.text: The food test for starch uses ___.
questions.explanation: Iodine solution turns blue-black in the presence of starch. Benedict's solution tests for reducing sugars.

questions.text: The enzyme ptyalin in saliva acts on ___.
questions.explanation: Ptyalin (salivary amylase) begins the digestion of starch, breaking it down to maltose.

questions.text: In mammals, oxygenated blood is carried from the lungs to the heart by the ___.
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein is the only vein that carries oxygenated blood, from the lungs to the left atrium.

questions.text: Water absorbed by the roots is transported to the leaves through the ___.
questions.explanation: The xylem vessels carry water and mineral salts upwards; the phloem carries manufactured food.

questions.text: The blood cells responsible for carrying oxygen are the ___.
questions.explanation: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds and carries oxygen.

questions.text: The movement of water molecules from a dilute solution to a concentrated solution through a semi-permeable membrane is ___.
questions.explanation: Osmosis is the movement of water molecules across a semi-permeable membrane from a dilute to a concentrated solution.

questions.text: The energy currency of the cell is ___.
questions.explanation: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) stores and supplies energy for cellular activities.

questions.text: Anaerobic respiration in yeast produces ___.
questions.explanation: Yeast ferments glucose to ethanol and carbon dioxide, releasing energy, when oxygen is absent.

questions.text: Gaseous exchange in mammals takes place in the ___.
questions.explanation: The alveoli are the thin-walled air sacs where oxygen and carbon dioxide are exchanged with the blood.

questions.text: The functional unit of the mammalian kidney is the ___.
questions.explanation: The nephron is the structural and functional unit of the kidney, filtering blood and forming urine.

questions.text: The main nitrogenous waste product excreted by mammals is ___.
questions.explanation: Mammals convert toxic ammonia to urea in the liver and excrete it in urine.

questions.text: The movement of a plant shoot towards light is called ___.
questions.explanation: Phototropism is growth towards light; shoots are positively phototropic.

questions.text: The joint between the humerus and the radius and ulna (the elbow) is a ___ joint.
questions.explanation: The elbow is a hinge joint, allowing movement in one plane like a door hinge.

questions.text: The plant hormone mainly responsible for cell elongation in shoots is ___.
questions.explanation: Auxins promote cell elongation in shoots and control tropic responses.

questions.text: The transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower is ___.
questions.explanation: Self-pollination is the transfer of pollen within the same flower (or the same plant).

questions.text: In flowering plants, double fertilization results in the formation of the ___.
questions.explanation: One male gamete fuses with the egg to form the zygote, while the other fuses with the polar nuclei to form the endosperm.

questions.text: Fertilization in mammals normally takes place in the ___.
questions.explanation: The sperm meets and fertilizes the ovum in the fallopian tube (oviduct).

questions.text: Which of the following is a form of asexual reproduction in Hydra?
questions.explanation: Hydra reproduces asexually by budding: a small outgrowth develops and detaches as a new individual.

questions.text: Epigeal germination differs from hypogeal germination in that in epigeal germination the ___.
options: cotyledons are carried above the soil
questions.explanation: In epigeal germination the cotyledons are carried above the ground (e.g. beans); in hypogeal germination they stay below (e.g. maize).

questions.text: Which of the following conditions is NOT generally necessary for seed germination?
questions.explanation: Seeds generally require water, oxygen and a suitable temperature; light is not a general requirement for germination.

questions.text: The part of the brain that controls balance and posture is the ___.
questions.explanation: The cerebellum coordinates movement, balance and posture.

questions.text: Insulin is produced by the ___.
options: islets of Langerhans in the pancreas
questions.explanation: The beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas secrete insulin, which lowers blood sugar.

questions.text: A simple reflex action such as withdrawing the hand from a hot object is controlled by the ___.
questions.explanation: The reflex arc passes through the spinal cord, producing a rapid response without involving conscious thought.

questions.text: The instrument used to measure the turbidity of water is the ___.
questions.explanation: The secchi disc is lowered into water to judge its clarity (turbidity).

questions.text: Which of the following is a biotic factor affecting the distribution of organisms?
questions.explanation: Predation is a biotic (living) factor; temperature, rainfall and soil pH are abiotic factors.

questions.text: The association between a tick and a cow is an example of ___.
questions.explanation: The tick benefits by feeding on the cow's blood while the cow is harmed, which is parasitism.

questions.text: In a food chain, green plants occupy the ___ trophic level.
questions.explanation: Green plants are producers and form the first trophic level, on which all other levels depend.

questions.text: The bacteria found in the root nodules of leguminous plants that fix atmospheric nitrogen are ___.
questions.explanation: Rhizobium bacteria in legume root nodules fix atmospheric nitrogen into forms plants can use.

questions.text: Mangrove swamps are characterized by ___.
options: waterlogged saline soils and stilt roots
questions.explanation: Mangroves grow in waterlogged, salty coastal soils, and their trees have stilt roots and breathing roots.

questions.text: Which of the following animals is adapted to arboreal life?
questions.explanation: Monkeys live in trees (arboreal life), with grasping limbs and tails adapted for climbing.

questions.text: The natural vegetation of southern Nigeria is mainly ___.
questions.explanation: Southern Nigeria, with its high rainfall, is covered mainly by tropical rainforest.

questions.text: The Guinea savanna lies between the ___.
questions.explanation: The Guinea savanna belt lies between the southern rainforest and the drier Sudan savanna to the north.

questions.text: Population density is defined as the number of individuals per unit ___.
questions.explanation: Population density = number of individuals divided by the area (or volume) they occupy.

questions.text: The orderly and progressive replacement of one community by another until a stable climax community is reached is called ___.
questions.explanation: Ecological succession is the gradual change in community composition over time towards a stable climax.

questions.text: Which soil type has the highest water-retaining capacity?
questions.explanation: Clay particles are the smallest and pack closely, so clayey soil holds the most water.

questions.text: The loss of soil nutrients by the downward movement of water through the soil is called ___.
questions.explanation: Leaching is the washing down of soluble nutrients below the reach of plant roots.

questions.text: Cholera is caused by ___.
questions.explanation: Cholera is caused by the bacterium Vibrio cholerae, spread through contaminated water and food.

questions.text: The Anopheles mosquito is the vector of ___.
questions.explanation: The female Anopheles mosquito transmits the Plasmodium parasite that causes malaria.

questions.text: Which of the following is a method of conserving soil fertility?
questions.explanation: Crop rotation, especially including legumes, restores soil nutrients; the other practices deplete them.

questions.text: Height in humans is an example of ___ variation.
questions.explanation: Height shows a continuous range of values influenced by many genes and the environment.

questions.text: A person with blood group O can donate red blood cells to a person with blood group ___.
questions.explanation: Group O red cells carry no A or B antigens, so group O is the universal red-cell donor.

questions.text: The chromosome number in a normal human body cell is ___.
questions.explanation: Human body (somatic) cells contain 46 chromosomes in 23 pairs; gametes contain 23.

questions.text: In a cross between two heterozygous tall plants (Tt x Tt), the expected phenotypic ratio of tall to short offspring is ___.
questions.explanation: The cross gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt: three tall phenotypes to one short, a 3:1 ratio.

questions.text: Haemophilia is a ___.
questions.explanation: Haemophilia is caused by a recessive gene carried on the X chromosome.

questions.text: The sex of a child is determined by the ___.
questions.explanation: The father's sperm carries either an X or a Y chromosome, which determines whether the child is female (XX) or male (XY).

questions.text: The theory of evolution by natural selection was proposed by ___.
questions.explanation: Charles Darwin proposed natural selection: organisms best adapted to their environment survive and reproduce.

questions.text: Lamarck's theory of evolution is based on the inheritance of ___.
questions.explanation: Lamarck proposed that characteristics acquired during an organism's lifetime could be inherited by its offspring.

questions.text: The fossil record provides evidence for evolution by showing ___.
options: that all organisms lived at the same time
the gradual changes in organisms over time
the exact age of the earth
questions.explanation: Fossils in successive rock layers show organisms changing gradually over geological time.
